title: In-band token stamps and offline reconcile pipeline for cache-aware latency attribution
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: deliver a lightweight, production-safe mechanism to record per-token wall-clock stamps in the serving path and an offline reconcile pipeline that attributes token-level latency and cost delta caused by KV/cache hits vs misses. This enables: 1) accurate per-token latency histograms (p50/p90/p99) for prefix vs generation tokens, 2) KV-cache delta scoring so we can quantify cost savings from cache hits, and 3) reconciliation between streaming/timing telemetry and billing records for customer-facing reporting.

Approach summary:
- In-band token stamps: add a compact per-token stamp to the request emission path (epoch microseconds + event tag) using a binary-compact encoding attached to request traces. The encoding is optional and controlled by route-level flags and sampling rate.
- Sampling strategy: default 0.5% per-request sampling, with config to bump to 5% for debug cycles. Sampling config aligns with token length bucketing to ensure long outputs are represented.
- Cache-delta scoring: each token stamp includes a KV-cache indicator (hit|miss|bypass) and a small counter for batch position so we can compute per-token delta when combined with micro-timings from the kernel scheduler.
- Offline reconcile pipeline: consume emitted stamps + serving micro-timings from the trace aggregator and the token accounting stream. Join and compute per-token wall_clock_time, kernel_time, queuing_time, and cache_delta_time. Produce aggregated stores by customer_id/model/route/sequence_length_bucket and export to metrics backend and billing ledger.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Must keep added overhead < 1% median p95 latency impact when sampling is off. When sampling on, target <5% overhead on p95 for sampled requests.
- Avoid increasing cardinality in metrics backend. Solution: keep stamps out of time-series metrics; produce aggregate rollups in pipeline and only materialize a fixed set of percentile keys.
- Privacy/compliance: token-level content is never emitted. Stamps are strict timing+flags only (no token text nor token ids).

Acceptance criteria:
- Stamps implementable in runtime with feature flag, gated by sampling rate.
- Reconcile job produces daily and hourly aggregates: per-model p50/p90/p99 per-token latency and % latency attributable to cache misses.
- Dashboard: new Token Attribution dashboard in Console showing model/route/token-position breakdowns with cost delta estimates.
- Verified overhead baseline: rollout validation tests show <=1% median latency change when sampling disabled and sampling telemetry matches synthetic ground-truth within 3% error on latency metrics.
comments: 2026-02-16: Initial design review with runtime and telemetry teams. Agreement to keep stamps binary-compact and not put them into Prometheus labels (avoid cardinality explosion). Action: Marco to prototype in local runtime branch.

2026-02-22: Prototype PoC (branch: feat/token-stamps) produces stamped trace events via the trace hook. Early numbers: sampled mode added ~2.8% p95 add on a 1k-token generation test. Need optimization in encoding path. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4182

2026-02-26: Design decision: use two-tier sampling (route-level sampling + length-bucket upsample). This mitigates bias toward short outputs. Added to spec doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Token+Stamps+Design

2026-03-03: Telemetry pipeline sketch done. We'll leverage existing trace-aggregator (kinesis->flink) to join stamps with microtimings and write aggregates to Druid. Pipeline draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-pipelines/pull/207
2026-03-09: Security review kickoff. Confirmed stamps contain no token text nor token ids. Need formal sign-off from Privacy (ticket PRIV-128).

2026-03-12: Internal demo of reconcile job running on a 24h synthetic replay (1M requests). Output aggregates match expected latency deltas within 2.1%. Next: create Console dashboard and rollout plan with canary sampling at 0.1%.
notes: Implementation will be phased: Phase 1 - in-band stamps + basic recon job + daily aggregates; Phase 2 - realtime join for nearline dashboards and alerting; Phase 3 - customer-facing per-route bill reconciliation export. Monitor SLOs closely during each phase.
recent_action: Canary plan drafted: enable sampling at 0.1% for 5% of production hosts for 48h, run reconcile job on that slice and compare to baseline billing traces. Responsible: Marco Liu.
customer_notes: This feature will allow us to explain per-request latency spikes and to quantify cost savings from KB/kv cache tuning; customers on Dedicated can request expanded sampling for their routes.
